cards.text: Abraham and Sarah have been waiting on a son. Years ago the LORD promised Sarah one, and when she heard it, she laughed to herself (Genesis 18:10-12). Now, friend, the LORD attends to Sarah.

cards.question: The LORD does for Sarah what He had promised.

cards.text: Sarah conceives and bears Abraham a son in his old age. God makes a promise and KEEPS it, which is more than I can say for me, because I promised the dead batteries I shared that drawer with we'd be out by spring, and friend, we were NOT.

cards.question: The LORD once said Sarah's son would come at a set time. When does Sarah's son arrive?

answers.text: At the very time God had promised
A full year after the promised time
Many years after the promised time

cards.text: Now this baby needs a name. And Abraham's the one picking it, no group chat vote, no list of forty options taped to the fridge.

cards.question: Abraham gives the name ___ to the son Sarah bore him.
Abraham waits until Isaac is a year old to circumcise him.
Abraham was ___ years old when his son Isaac was born to him.

cards.text: Then Sarah says God has made her laugh. I bet the last time she laughed it was the 'yeah, right' kind, but THIS laugh? Whole different recipe.

cards.question: Sarah says God has made her laugh. Who does she say will laugh with her?

cards.text: Sarah adds that nobody would have told Abraham she'd ever nurse children, yet she's borne him a son. Not the neighbors, not the group chat, NOBODY had this on their calendar.
The child grows and gets weaned. And Abraham marks the day.

cards.question: How does Abraham mark the day Isaac is weaned?

answers.text: He offers a sacrifice at Bethel

cards.text: Quick reminder: Hagar is Sarah's Egyptian maidservant, and she bore Abraham a son named Ishmael (Genesis 16:1, 15). Now Sarah sees what Hagar's son is doing to her son Isaac.

cards.question: What does Sarah see Hagar's son doing to Isaac?
Sarah goes to Abraham and tells him to send Hagar and her son away.
Sarah says the slave woman's son will never share in the ___ with her son Isaac.

cards.text: This hits Abraham hard. The matter distresses him greatly, because it concerns his son Ishmael.
Then God tells Abraham, "Do not be distressed about the boy and your maidservant."

cards.question: God tells Abraham to listen to everything Sarah tells him. What reason does God give?

answers.text: Abraham's offspring will be reckoned through Isaac

cards.question: God tells Abraham that nothing will come of the slave woman's son.

cards.text: Early in the morning, Abraham gets up and puts bread and a skin of water on Hagar's shoulders. Then he sends her away with the boy.

cards.question: Hagar leaves and wanders. In which wilderness?

cards.text: Then the water in the skin is gone. Hagar leaves the boy under one of the bushes.

cards.question: Hagar goes and sits down about a bowshot away from the boy. Why does she say she's sitting that far off?

answers.text: She cannot bear to watch him die
She wants to search for water
She wants to pray by herself

cards.text: As she sits there, Hagar lifts up her voice and weeps. Then the angel of God calls to her from heaven, "What is wrong, Hagar?" and tells her not to be afraid.

cards.question: The angel tells Hagar that God has heard the voice of the boy.
The angel tells Hagar to get up and take the boy by the hand, because God will make him into a great ___.
Then God opens Hagar's eyes. What does she see?

cards.text: She goes, fills the skin with water and gives the boy a drink. I know a little something about thinking it's all over in the dark, friend, and then the light shows up.

cards.question: God is with the boy, and he grows up in the wilderness and becomes a great ___.
While Ishmael is living in the Wilderness of Paran, his mother gets him a wife from the land of ___.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend. Abraham's story still has PLENTY of time left on the timer.

findings.problem: "Years ago the LORD promised Sarah one" contradicts the cited text. Genesis 18:10 and 18:14 set the son's birth for about a year later ("At the appointed time I will return to you—in about a year"), not years later. The promise in Genesis 18:10 was also spoken to Abraham while Sarah listened at the tent entrance. It was not spoken to Sarah.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The joke adds something new to his backstory: he promised the dead batteries they'd be out by spring. That is a new event in the drawer. It is not a small moment or habit around his bakery.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The question states a Bible fact from outside the passage with no reference: "The LORD once said Sarah's son would come at a set time" (Genesis 17:21; 18:14).

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: This choice card follows another choice card, but no card has told the setup. Circumcision and the eight-day command (Genesis 17:12) never come up, so the baker has nothing to reason from.

rule.text: Not every choice card needs its own story card right before it: a choice card can follow another choice card when the setup is already told.

findings.problem: "NOBODY had this on their calendar" says something the passage shows is not so. Genesis 21:2 says the son came "at the very time God had promised," so God had set the time.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Ishmael has mocked his brother" is true in the passage (Genesis 21:9). A baker could argue it is God's reason.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. It is noticeably longer than the other two and is the only one with Bible-sounding wording ("reckoned").

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Most of the story cards in this stop are plain retellings with almost none of Papa Dorin's voice (cards 5, 6, 9, 11 and 13). The stop can stay serious during the hard moments, but card 6, for example, is only a bare quote.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
